name: StoreMy
tagline: A production-grade relational database built from scratch in Go 🗄️
summary: A complete relational database written in Go — slotted-page storage, Two-Phase Locking, write-ahead logging and a cost-based query optimizer.
description: Most developers use databases as black boxes — StoreMy tears the box open. It implements the complete RDBMS stack without any external database libraries: a slotted-page storage engine, Two-Phase Locking with deadlock detection, Write-Ahead Logging for crash recovery, a cost-based query optimizer, and a terminal UI — all across ~100,000 lines of Go organized into 13 strict architectural layers.
keyFeatures: Storage Engine: 4KB slotted-page heap files with a 4MB LRU buffer pool (O(1) eviction via HashMap + doubly-linked list), a B+Tree index with doubly-linked leaf pages for O(log n + k) range scans, and a Hash index for O(1) equality lookups.

ACID Transaction Engine: Two-Phase Locking at page granularity with a wait-for dependency graph that gates deadlock prevention before a transaction ever blocks — combined with NO-STEAL/FORCE buffer policies that eliminate the undo phase of crash recovery.

SQL Query Engine: Recursive-descent SQL parser building a full AST, a cost-based optimizer using catalog statistics (selectivity, cardinality, distinct values) to select among Hash Join O(n+m), Sort-Merge Join O(n log n), and Block Nested Loop — all executing via a streaming DbIterator chain.

Self-Describing System Catalog: All metadata (table schemas, indexes, statistics) stored as ordinary heap files in 6 catalog tables — the same 4KB slotted-page format as user tables — with a background goroutine refreshing cost estimates every 30 seconds.

keyFeatures: Complete Language Implementation Pipeline: Hand-crafted lexer supporting f-strings and multi-line comments. Pratt parser implementation with operator precedence and error recovery. Tree-walking evaluator supporting closures, OOP, and first-class functions. Standard library with 20+ built-in functions including map, filter, and reduce.

Interactive Step-by-Step Debugger: State tracking system capturing environment snapshots at every step. Visualized call stack and variable inspection for deep debugging. Time-travel navigation (forward/backward) with sub-millisecond transitions.

Real-Time AST Visualization Engine: React-based tree renderer supporting 15+ distinct AST node types. Bidirectional code-to-AST highlighting via Monaco decorations API. Live syntax processing with <100ms latency using memoized parsing.

Monaco-Powered Code Editor: Custom syntax highlighting and intelligent tokenization for 30+ types. Error underlining with precise source context extraction. Responsive split-pane and mobile drawer layouts via Tailwind and Shadcn UI.

name: SourceControl
tagline: Production-grade Git implementation from scratch in pure Go 🔧
summary: Git reimplemented in Go from the object store up — Merkle trees, binary index format and a real CLI, with a 121% test-to-code ratio.
description: Fully-functional version control system reimplementing Git's core internals in Go without wrapping git commands. Implements content-addressable object storage, Merkle tree structures, binary index format, and complete CLI with 16,354 lines of tests achieving 121% test-to-code ratio for production reliability.
keyFeatures: Content-Addressable Object Store with SHA-1: Custom implementation of Git's sharded directory structure (`.source/objects/ab/cdef...`). Type-safe wrappers for `ObjectHash`, `CompressedData`, and `SerializedObject`. Atomic write operations using the write-rename pattern to prevent corruption.

Concurrent Tree Building with Adaptive Parallelism: Generic worker pool using Go 1.18+ generics with panic recovery and context cancellation. Smart concurrency thresholds that dynamically trigger parallel processing via `errgroup`. Recursive conversion of hierarchical file systems into Git's flat tree object model.

Binary Index Format with O(1) Lookups: Dual data structure approach maintaining both a sorted slice (for compatibility) and a hash map. Optimized `entryMap` enabling constant-time file lookups during staging operations. Full SHA-1 checksum validation and atomic serialization to disk.

Type-Safe Path System and Config Hierarchy: Strongly-typed path abstractions (`AbsolutePath`, `RepositoryPath`) preventing mixing bugs. Thread-safe hierarchical config manager with 5-level precedence (CLI → repo → user → system → defaults). Concurrent config file loading protected by `RWMutex` and `errgroup`.

name: Reducer
tagline: Educational Redux reimplementation teaching state management internals 📚
summary: Redux rebuilt from scratch in TypeScript — middleware composition, slice reducers, Immer updates — to show how it actually works.
description: TypeScript-native state management library built from scratch to demystify Redux architecture. Implements core Redux patterns including middleware composition, slice-based reducers, and immutable updates using Immer, serving as both a functional library and educational resource for understanding state management internals.
keyFeatures: Type-Safe Store with Immutability: Custom Store class implementing the single-source-of-truth observer pattern. Strict `Object.freeze` enforcement for immutable state access. Built-in reentrancy protection to prevent dangerous nested dispatches. Reference equality checks within `combineReducers` for performance optimization.

Redux Toolkit-Style Slice Architecture: Immer integration allowing mutable logic to produce immutable state updates. `createSlice` API that auto-generates namespaced action creators. Support for `extraReducers` handling cross-slice state dependencies.

Composable Middleware System: Implementation of the triple-function currying pattern (`store => next => action`). Functional middleware composition pipeline using custom `reduce` logic. Full capability for async operations, logging, and action transformation.

Advanced TypeScript Type System: Generic `GenerateActionCreators` utility for automatic inference from reducers. Type-safe `ActionHandler` definitions using Immer's Draft types. Custom `isActionOf` type guards ensuring runtime and compile-time safety.

keyFeatures: Type-Safe Fluent Pipeline API: Chainable interface leveraging Go 1.18+ generics for compile-time safety. Support for Map/Filter/Reduce transformations and LINQ-style aliases. Lazy evaluation architecture delaying execution until terminal operations.

Reactive Flow Control Primitives: Advanced implementations of Throttle, Debounce, and FixedInterval pacing. Smart Batch grouping based on dynamic size or timeout triggers. Zero-allocation optimizations using timer reuse and state machine patterns.

description: Chrome extension that blocks distracting websites through a progressive 4-stage behavioral challenge system. name: gopool
tagline: A High-Performance Worker Pool for Go 🚀
summary: A generics-based Go worker pool with seven interchangeable scheduling strategies, including an LMAX Disruptor.
description: A type-safe, production-ready worker pool library built on Go 1.18+ generics. It exposes a single, unified API with 7 interchangeable scheduling strategies including an LMAX Disruptor implementation for sub-microsecond latency.
keyFeatures: Generic, Type-Safe API: Compile-time type safety with zero `interface{}` casts. Supports processing slices, maps, or streaming channels. Context-first API honoring cancellation and deadlines.

7 Interchangeable Scheduling Strategies: Financial-grade LMAX Disruptor for sub-microsecond latency. Work-Stealing deque using the Chase-Lev algorithm. Bitmask dispatch and Priority Queue for SLA-driven processing.
Resilience & Reliability: Automatic retry with configurable exponential backoff. Native token bucket rate limiting to prevent downstream overload. Per-worker panic recovery preventing pool crashes.
Advanced Performance Tuning: 1M+ tasks/sec peak throughput over 16 cores. Cache-line padded ring buffers eliminating false sharing. Linux CPU affinity pinning via `SchedSetaffinity`.
